expectations.text: Identifies the locked, greyed-out Pro tab behind a license key as trialware banned by the directory guidelines
expectations.evidence: "Locked UI shipped in the plugin is trialware (Rule 1)" and "A key that unlocks local code is banned"

expectations.text: Identifies the 14-day trial that disables itself inside the plugin as banned (functionality disabled after a trial period)
expectations.evidence: "14-day trial that switches itself off in the plugin | Time-limited features are trialware"

expectations.text: Recommends enforcing the Pro plan in the Formline service (API returns plan or quota limits) rather than in plugin code
expectations.evidence: "Start the trial in your service... The plugin shows 'N days left' from the API"; "Count and enforce in your service"

expectations.text: Offers a separate premium add-on sold and hosted outside WordPress.org as the alternative for features that must run locally
expectations.evidence: "If variant swapping must run in local PHP or JS, rung 2 (a premium add-on) moves up." It does not say the add-on is sold outside WordPress.org, so this is a thin pass.

expectations.text: Ranks the paid-value options with service-side enforcement as the default for a SaaS
expectations.evidence: "Paid-value verdict: rung 1... It is one codebase and one review, and it's the default for a SaaS."

expectations.text: Tells the user to remove Pro-only code and named Pro feature stubs from the directory plugin, not just hide them
expectations.evidence: "Named-but-absent pro features in free code read as trialware to reviewers, so don't leave them in the code as stubs"; checklist item 1 "Remove the greyed Pro UI, license-key unlock and local trial logic"

expectations.text: States that the free plugin may link to the paid offer but must not install the add-on or premium code itself
expectations.evidence: The transcript only mentions a link to the pricing page. It never says the plugin must not install or update premium code.

expectations.text: Limits upgrade prompts to the plugin's own settings page or contextual spots, with any site-wide notice dismissible
expectations.evidence: "show one contextual upgrade note on your settings page, with a link to your pricing page." Dismissibility is not mentioned, so this is a thin pass.

expectations.text: Requires an External services section in the readme naming the Formline API, data sent, when, and terms and privacy links
expectations.evidence: The "External services draft" names api.formline.example, the data sent, the trigger (after an administrator connects), and terms and privacy links.

expectations.text: Notes the 500-submission free quota is acceptable only when the service enforces it, not a local counter in the plugin
expectations.evidence: "Fine only if the service counts it... Count and enforce in your service."

expectations.text: Does not propose a license-key validation endpoint as the 'service' that unlocks local code
expectations.evidence: "Replace it with an account connection (OAuth or an account API key) that only identifies the site to Formline"
